record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: What are the convolution multipliers φ∗ : KH → KH , where KH is the subclass of functions f in SH with convex images f (D)? A particularly interesting case is the radius of convexity problem: for which values of r in (0, 1)pis the function z 7→ f (rz) convex in D, when f is convex in D? (It is known that r ≤ (2) − 1, see Clunie and Sheil-Small [167].) (T. Sheil-Small)

evidence.quote: What are the convolution multipliers φ∗ : KH → KH , where KH is the subclass of functions f in SH with convex images f (D)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. A complex-valued harmonic function $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ admits a unique decomposition $f=h+\overline{g}$, where $h$ and $g$ are analytic on $\mathbb{D}$ with $g(0)=0$. Let $S_H$ be the class of all such harmonic functions $f$ that are univalent and sense-preserving on $\mathbb{D}$ and normalized by $h(0)=g(0)=0$ and $h'(0)=1$. Let $K_H\subset S_H$ be the subclass consisting of those $f\in S_H$ for which the image $f(\mathbb{D})$ is a convex domain.

For two harmonic functions $f_1=h_1+\overline{g_1}$ and $f_2=h_2+\overline{g_2}$ on $\mathbb{D}$, define their (Hadamard) convolution by
$$f_1 * f_2 = h_1 * h_2 + \overline{g_1 * g_2},$$
where for analytic functions $a(z)=\sum a_n z^n$ and $b(z)=\sum b_n z^n$ the convolution is $a*b(z)=\sum a_n b_n z^n$.

(a) Characterize all harmonic functions $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{D}$ (the "convolution multipliers") such that the map $f\mapsto \varphi * f$ sends $K_H$ into $K_H$.

(b) (Radius of convexity for $K_H$.) Determine the largest $r_0\in(0,1)$ such that for every $f\in K_H$ the dilated function $z\mapsto f(rz)$ has convex image in $\mathbb{D}$ for all $0<r\le r_0$. It is known that $r_0\ge \sqrt{2}-1$; determine the exact value of $r_0$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on harmonic convex univalent mappings, convolution multipliers, and radius of convexity yield numerous partial results (e.g., Dorff, Ruscheweyh–Sheil-Small, and others on convolutions of planar harmonic convex mappings), but no source found gives a complete characterization of multipliers $\varphi*:K_H\to K_H$ or an exact value for the radius of convexity beyond the lower bound $\sqrt{2}-1$ established by Clunie and Sheil-Small. The problem appears to remain open in its full form.

status_evidence.title: Convolutions of planar harmonic convex mappings (Dorff)
status_evidence.snippet: In the harmonic case, the convolution of two convex harmonic mappings need not be univalent; partial results are obtained under additional hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results on convolutions within K_H are known.

status_evidence.title: Classes of harmonic functions defined by convolution
status_evidence.snippet: Studies radii of convexity and starlikeness for subclasses of harmonic functions defined by convolution.
status_evidence.claim: Radius-of-convexity questions for harmonic convex mappings remain an active area with only partial answers.
